package_info.why_malicious: The API implementation lacked proper object-level authorization, allowing any user—including unauthenticated users—to access and modify other users' preferences and sensitive metadata. This resulted in both unauthorized data exposure and manipulation, violating user privacy, data integrity, and platform trust.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP GET request to API endpoint)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a GET request is made to the userPreferences API endpoint with a specified user ID and preference type, the server retrieves and returns the corresponding user's preferences and metadata to any requester, resulting in unauthorized data exposure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The endpoint returns user-specific preference data to any requester, regardless of authentication or authorization, exposing sensitive information to unauthorized parties.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict access to user preferences so that only the authenticated user or authorized parties can retrieve their own data. Here, any user can access any other user's preferences by specifying their user ID.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate use case would be an authenticated user retrieving their own preferences via a GET request to this endpoint, with proper authorization checks enforced.
key_indicators: No authentication or authorization required for API access
User ID is directly specifiable in the URL path
Sensitive metadata (such as activity timestamps and course IDs) is exposed in the response
Endpoint responds to requests from anonymous or unauthenticated sessions

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP PUT request to API endpoint)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a PUT request with a crafted JSON payload is sent to the userPreferences API endpoint specifying a user ID and preference type, the server updates or overwrites the target user's preferences and metadata without verifying the requester's identity, resulting in unauthorized data manipulation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The endpoint allows any requester to modify another user's preferences and activity metadata without authentication or authorization, enabling arbitrary data tampering.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict modification of user preferences to the authenticated user or authorized parties, ensuring only the owner can update their data. Here, any user can alter any other user's preferences by specifying their user ID.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate use case would be an authenticated user updating their own preferences via a PUT request, with strict authorization checks in place.
key_indicators: No authentication or authorization required for modifying user data
User ID is directly specifiable in the URL path
Ability to arbitrarily set or overwrite another user's preferences and metadata
Endpoint accepts and processes requests from anonymous or unauthenticated sessions

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a GET request to the userPreferences API endpoint with a target user ID and preference type to enumerate or exfiltrate user preference data and metadata.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access to sensitive user data, resulting in a privacy violation and potential for further targeted attacks.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a PUT request to the same API endpoint with a crafted payload to overwrite or manipulate the target user's preferences and activity metadata.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can bias user experience, manipulate recommendations, or further exploit the platform by corrupting user data.

behavioral_signatures: API requests to userPreferences endpoints where the user ID in the path does not match the authenticated session user
Anonymous or unauthenticated requests to /api/userPreferences.v1/ endpoints
Unusual frequency or volume of GET or PUT requests to userPreferences API endpoints, especially targeting multiple user IDs
PUT requests to userPreferences API with payloads modifying preferences for users other than the session user
network_indicators: Unusual or unauthenticated traffic to www.coursera.org/api/userPreferences.v1/*
PUT requests to userPreferences API from non-logged-in or anonymous sessions
GET or PUT requests to userPreferences API with mismatched user ID and session user
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor API logs for GET and PUT requests to /api/userPreferences.v1/ where the user ID in the URL does not match the authenticated session user, or where requests are made without authentication. Flag and alert on any requests to this endpoint from anonymous users or from users accessing or modifying IDs other than their own. Implement rate-limiting and review for bulk or automated access patterns to this endpoint. Correlate with session authentication logs to identify unauthorized access or modification attempts.
